w001.def: A portion is one part or share of something larger.
w001.ex1: Ratchet gave every Autobot a small portion of energon before the long trip.
w001.ex2: I ate a big portion of spaghetti at dinner.

w002.def: If something is scarce, there is very little of it and it is hard to find.
w002.ex1: Energon became scarce on Cybertron, so the Autobots had to share it carefully.
w002.ex2: Fresh water is scarce in the desert.

w003.def: Numerous means many or very many.
w003.ex1: Optimus Prime stayed calm even though numerous Decepticons gathered on the ridge.
w003.ex2: The sky was full of numerous stars last night.

w004.def: Sufficient means as much as you need.
w004.ex1: Wheeljack checked that the Autobots had sufficient energon for the trip home.
w004.ex2: Is there sufficient paper for the whole class?

w005.def: A supply is an amount of something kept for later use, and to supply is to give someone what they need.
w005.ex1: Ratchet kept a large supply of repair tools inside the Ark.
w005.ex2: The school will supply pencils for the big test.

w006.def: Vast means extremely large in size or amount.
w006.ex1: Bumblebee gazed across the vast plains of Cybertron.
w006.ex2: The ocean looked vast from the top of the cliff.

w007.def: Enormous means much bigger than normal.
w007.ex1: Ironhide pulled an enormous cargo crate across the base.
w007.ex2: An enormous wave rolled onto the beach.

w008.def: Miniature means very small, and a miniature is a tiny copy of something bigger.
w008.ex1: Wheeljack built a miniature Ark that fit on his workbench.
w008.ex2: She keeps a miniature of the Eiffel Tower on her shelf.
w008.root: Italian miniatura — Latin miniare (to color with red lead)

w009.def: To enlarge something is to make it bigger.
w009.ex1: Perceptor used his lens to enlarge the tiny map on his screen.
w009.ex2: We will enlarge the photo so everyone can see it.
w009.root: Old French en- (make) + large — Latin largus (abundant)

w010.def: Slight means small in amount or not very serious.
w010.ex1: Jazz felt a slight bump as the Autobots landed.
w010.ex2: There is a slight chance of rain this afternoon.

w011.def: Swift means moving or happening very fast.
w011.ex1: Bumblebee made a swift dash across the battlefield.
w011.ex2: The swift runner won the race easily.

w012.def: Gradually means little by little over a long time.
w012.ex1: The sky above Cybertron gradually turned from gray to gold.
w012.ex2: The ice gradually melted in the warm sun.

w013.def: A hasty choice is one made too fast without careful thought.
w013.ex1: Optimus Prime warned the team not to make a hasty decision.
w013.ex2: I made a hasty guess on the quiz and got it wrong.

w014.ex1: Jazz had a hard time flying over Cybertron because of the frequent storms.
w014.ex2: Our dog makes frequent trips to the water bowl.

w015.def: A moment is a very short amount of time.
w015.ex1: For one moment, Optimus Prime stood completely still.
w015.ex2: Wait just a moment while I tie my shoe.

w016.def: To plead is to ask for something in a very serious or emotional way.
w016.ex1: Bumblebee began to plead with Optimus Prime to let him join the team.
w016.ex2: I had to plead with my mom for five more minutes at the park.

w017.def: To coax is to gently and patiently get someone to do something.
w017.ex1: Wheeljack tried to coax the shy robot out from behind the crates.
w017.ex2: She had to coax the kitten down from the tree with a treat.

w018.def: To murmur is to speak in a very low, soft voice, and a murmur is that quiet sound.
w018.ex1: Perceptor began to murmur quietly as he worked on the puzzle.
w018.ex2: A murmur of excitement ran through the crowd.
w018.root: Latin murmur — a low humming sound

w019.def: To exclaim is to say something suddenly and loudly because you are surprised or excited.
w019.ex1: Bumblebee was about to exclaim with joy when he spotted the lost energon cube.
w019.ex2: We all exclaim with joy when the fireworks begin.
w019.root: Latin exclamare — ex (out) + clamare (to cry out)

w020.def: A rumor is a story that people pass along that may not be true.
w020.ex1: A rumor spread across Cybertron that the Decepticons had lost their leader.
w020.ex2: There was a rumor at school that we would get a snow day.

w021.def: To ponder is to think about something carefully for a long time.
w021.ex1: Perceptor will ponder the problem all night before he gives an answer.
w021.ex2: I like to ponder what it would be like to live on the moon.

w022.def: To analyze is to study something closely by looking at each of its parts.
w022.ex1: Perceptor used his scanner to analyze the strange signal.
w022.ex2: Scientists analyze rocks to learn how old they are.

w023.def: To assume is to believe something is true without checking.
w023.ex1: "Do not assume the Decepticons are gone just because the base is quiet," said Optimus Prime.
w023.ex2: I assume the bus is late because of the snow.

w024.def: If you are curious, you want to learn or know more about something.
w024.ex1: Bumblebee was curious about the glowing device on Wheeljack's desk.
w024.ex2: The curious puppy sniffed every corner of the room.

w025.def: A notion is an idea or belief about something.
w025.ex1: Optimus Prime rejected the notion that the Autobots should give up.
w025.ex2: She had a notion that the cat was hiding in the closet.

w026.def: A valiant person is brave and determined even when things are hard.
w026.ex1: Optimus Prime made a valiant stand to protect his team.
w026.ex2: The valiant knight saved the village in the story.

w027.def: A timid person is shy and easily scared.
w027.ex1: The timid little robot hid behind Ironhide when the thunder rumbled.
w027.ex2: The timid rabbit ran back into its hole.

w028.def: To hesitate is to pause before acting because you feel unsure.
w028.ex1: Jazz did not hesitate when Optimus Prime called for help.
w028.ex2: Do not hesitate to ask the teacher if you are confused.

w029.def: To tremble is to shake a little because you are scared, cold, or excited.
w029.ex1: Wheeljack felt the ground tremble as the giant machine rolled closer.
w029.ex2: My hands tremble when I stand up to give a speech.

w030.def: To dread something is to be very afraid of what will happen, and dread is that strong fear.
w030.ex1: The little Autobots dread the long dark tunnels under Cybertron.
w030.ex2: She felt a sense of dread before walking onto the stage.

w031.def: If you are eager, you want very much to do or get something.
w031.ex1: Bumblebee was eager to go with Optimus Prime on the trip.
w031.ex2: The eager students lined up to see the science show.

w032.ex1: The weary Autobots rested after their long march across the desert.
w032.ex2: The weary hikers sat down by the trail.

w033.def: Gloomy means dark and sad, or feeling without hope.
w033.ex1: Ratchet felt gloomy when rain clouds covered the sky.
w033.ex2: The gloomy weather kept us indoors all day.

w034.def: A frantic person is so worried or rushed that they cannot stay calm.
w034.ex1: Wheeljack made a frantic search for the missing blueprint.
w034.ex2: We made a frantic dash to catch the bus.

w035.def: Delight is great joy, and to delight someone is to please them very much.
w035.ex1: Bumblebee jumped with delight when he saw his friends return.
w035.ex2: The magician will delight the children with a new trick.

w036.def: A humble person does not brag or think they are better than others.
w036.ex1: Even after saving the city, Optimus Prime stayed humble.
w036.ex2: The humble champion thanked her team before taking any credit.

w037.def: Generosity is the quality of giving freely to others.
w037.ex1: The Autobots thanked Ratchet for his generosity when he shared his last energon.
w037.ex2: Her generosity made the class food drive a big success.

w038.def: A loyal friend stays faithful and supports you no matter what.
w038.ex1: Ironhide stayed loyal to Optimus Prime through every battle.
w038.ex2: Our loyal dog waits by the door every afternoon.
w038.root: Old French loial — Latin legalis (of the law)

w039.def: A courteous person is polite and shows respect to others.
w039.ex1: Jazz was courteous to the visitors and showed them around the base.
w039.ex2: It is courteous to say thank you after a meal.

w040.def: To cooperate is to work together with others to reach a goal.
w040.ex1: The Autobots must cooperate to lift the heavy beam.
w040.ex2: Our class must cooperate to finish the giant puzzle.

w041.def: A stubborn person refuses to change their mind even when they should.
w041.ex1: Ironhide was stubborn and would not take a different route.
w041.ex2: The stubborn mule would not walk up the hill.

w042.def: An arrogant person acts as if they are better or more important than everyone else.
w042.ex1: The arrogant Decepticon bragged that no one could ever beat him.
w042.ex2: The arrogant player ignored the advice of his coach.
w042.root: Latin arrogare — ad (to) + rogare (to ask, claim)

w043.def: A greedy person wants much more than they need.
w043.ex1: A greedy Decepticon tried to keep all the energon for himself.
w043.ex2: The greedy boy took all the cookies and left none for his sister.

w044.def: Mischief is playful behavior that causes trouble but not serious harm.
w044.ex1: Jazz was up to mischief when he painted Ironhide's wheels bright orange.
w044.ex2: The puppy got into mischief and chewed my sock.

w045.def: To boast is to brag by talking too proudly about what you have or can do.
w045.ex1: The Decepticon would boast about his speed to anyone who would listen.
w045.ex2: My cousin likes to boast about how many goals he scored.

w046.def: To assist is to help someone do something.
w046.ex1: Wheeljack will assist Ratchet with the repairs.
w046.ex2: A teacher may assist you with a hard math problem.

w047.def: A benefit is something that helps you or gives you an advantage, and to benefit is to be helped by something.
w047.ex1: One benefit of Bumblebee's small size is that he can fit into tiny places.
w047.ex2: Plants benefit from sunlight and water.

w048.def: To rescue is to save someone from danger, and a rescue is the act of saving.
w048.ex1: The Autobots rush to rescue their friend from the collapsing tunnel.
w048.ex2: The rescue of the lost hikers took all night.

w049.def: To deprive someone is to take away something they need or want.
w049.ex1: The Decepticons tried to deprive Cybertron of its last energon.
w049.ex2: Staying up too late can deprive you of sleep.

w050.def: To hinder is to get in the way and make something harder to do.
w050.ex1: Deep mud will hinder the Autobots as they roll toward the base.
w050.ex2: Heavy backpacks can hinder a hiker on a steep trail.
w050.root: Old English hindrian — to hold back

w051.def: To alter something is to change it a little.
w051.ex1: Wheeljack had to alter the blueprint after Perceptor found a mistake.
w051.ex2: My mom will alter my coat so the sleeves are shorter.

w052.def: To adapt is to change so you can fit a new situation.
w052.ex1: The Autobots had to adapt quickly to the cold, icy planet.
w052.ex2: Polar bears adapt to freezing weather with thick fur.

w053.def: To modify something is to change part of it to make it better or different.
w053.ex1: Wheeljack will modify Bumblebee's engine so it runs quieter.
w053.ex2: We can modify the recipe by adding less sugar.

w054.def: A substitute is a person or thing that takes the place of another, and to substitute is to put one thing in place of another.
w054.ex1: Ironhide acted as the substitute driver when Jazz was sick.
w054.ex2: You can substitute honey for sugar in the recipe.
w054.root: Latin substituere — sub (in place of) + statuere (to set up)

w055.def: A transition is a change from one state, place, or activity to another.
w055.ex1: The transition from the old base to the new one took the Autobots three days.
w055.ex2: It took a while for me to make the transition to the new school.

w056.def: To launch is to send something off or start something new, and a launch is that start.
w056.ex1: Wheeljack will launch the rescue ship at dawn.
w056.ex2: The launch of the rocket drew a huge crowd.

w057.def: To halt is to stop, and a halt is a stop.
w057.ex1: Optimus Prime raised his hand to halt the convoy.
w057.ex2: The bus came to a sudden halt at the red light.
w057.root: German halten — to hold, to stop

w058.def: To resume is to begin again after a pause.
w058.ex1: The Autobots will resume their journey once the storm passes.
w058.ex2: Class will resume after the fire drill.
w058.root: Latin resumere — re (again) + sumere (to take up)

w059.def: Abruptly means suddenly and without warning.
w059.ex1: The engine of Jazz's car stopped abruptly, and everyone turned to look.
w059.ex2: The music stopped abruptly when the power went out.

w060.def: To abolish something is to end it completely, often by an official rule.
w060.ex1: Optimus Prime asked the council to abolish the unfair rule.
w060.ex2: The town voted to abolish the old law against skateboarding.

w061.def: Something obvious is easy to see or understand.
w061.ex1: It was obvious to Perceptor that the signal came from the north.
w061.ex2: The answer was obvious once I saw the picture.
w061.root: Latin obvius — ob (in the way of) + via (road)

w062.def: Something vague is not clear or exact.
w062.ex1: Jazz gave a vague answer, so Ratchet asked him to explain again.
w062.ex2: I have only a vague memory of that trip.

w063.def: If something is apparent, it is clear and easy to see.
w063.ex1: It soon became apparent that Bumblebee was the fastest Autobot on the team.
w063.ex2: It was apparent from the muddy floor that someone had come inside.

w064.def: To baffle someone is to confuse them so much that they cannot figure something out.
w064.ex1: The strange symbols on the wall baffle even Perceptor.
w064.ex2: The magician's trick will baffle the whole audience.

w065.def: To clarify is to make something easier to understand.
w065.ex1: Optimus Prime paused to clarify the plan so everyone understood it.
w065.ex2: Can you clarify what you mean by that word?

w066.def: An antique is something very old that is valued because of its age.
w066.ex1: Wheeljack found an antique energon cube hidden in the ruins of Cybertron.
w066.ex2: My grandmother keeps an antique clock in her hall.

w067.def: An ancestor is a family member who lived long ago, before you.
w067.ex1: Optimus Prime honored the ancestor who built the first Autobot city.
w067.ex2: My ancestor sailed across the ocean more than two hundred years ago.

w068.def: A tradition is a custom or belief passed down from older people to younger ones.
w068.ex1: It is an Autobot tradition to share energon before a big trip.
w068.ex2: Our family has a tradition of baking pies on the first snow day.

w069.def: Something obsolete is no longer used because something newer has replaced it.
w069.ex1: Wheeljack's old scanner was obsolete after Perceptor built a better one.
w069.ex2: Rotary phones are obsolete because almost everyone uses a cell phone.

w070.def: A novice is a person who is just beginning to learn something.
w070.ex1: Bumblebee was still a novice when he first drove with the Autobots.
w070.ex2: As a novice chess player, I lost my first ten games.

w071.def: To deceive is to make someone believe something that is not true.
w071.ex1: The Decepticon used a fake signal to deceive the Autobots.
w071.ex2: Magicians use quick hands to deceive the audience.

w072.def: To disguise is to change how something looks to hide what it really is, and a disguise is what you use to do that.
w072.ex1: Bumblebee can disguise himself as a small yellow car.
w072.ex2: She wore a pirate disguise to the party.
w072.root: Old French desguiser — des- (away) + guise (way of dressing)

w073.def: Something authentic is real and not a copy.
w073.ex1: Perceptor tested the energon crystal to prove it was authentic.
w073.ex2: The museum has an authentic dinosaur bone.

w074.def: To reveal is to show something that was hidden or secret.
w074.ex1: Optimus Prime will reveal the secret plan to the team at sunrise.
w074.ex2: The magician will reveal what is hidden under the cloth.

w075.def: An illusion is something that looks real but is not.
w075.ex1: The Decepticon army was only an illusion made of light.
w075.ex2: The pond in the desert was only an illusion caused by the heat.

w076.def: A compromise is an agreement where each side gives up something, and to compromise is to reach that kind of agreement.
w076.ex1: Optimus Prime and Ironhide reached a compromise about which road to take.
w076.ex2: We had to compromise and let each person pick one movie.

w077.def: A dispute is a serious disagreement, and to dispute is to say that something is wrong.
w077.ex1: The two Autobots had a dispute over who should drive first.
w077.ex2: I will not dispute the score because the referee was right.

w078.def: To persuade is to convince someone to do or believe something by giving good reasons.
w078.ex1: Bumblebee tried to persuade Ratchet to let him test the new engine.
w078.ex2: I will try to persuade my parents to adopt a dog.

w079.def: To oppose is to be against something and try to stop it.
w079.ex1: The Decepticons oppose the Autobots' plan to protect Cybertron.
w079.ex2: Many neighbors oppose the plan to cut down the old oak tree.

w080.def: If a group is unanimous, every single person agrees.
w080.ex1: The Autobots made a unanimous vote to follow Optimus Prime.
w080.ex2: The class was unanimous in choosing a picnic for the party.

w081.ex1: The feeble light from Wheeljack's old lamp barely lit the tunnel.
w081.ex2: The sick puppy gave a feeble bark.

w082.def: Something flimsy is thin or weak and can break easily.
w082.ex1: The flimsy bridge shook under Ironhide's heavy tires.
w082.ex2: My flimsy umbrella broke in the wind.

w083.def: If you are vulnerable, you can be easily hurt or harmed.
w083.ex1: Bumblebee felt vulnerable without his armor.
w083.ex2: Baby birds are vulnerable to hungry cats.

w084.def: Vigor is strong energy and healthy strength.
w084.ex1: Optimus Prime charged into the work with great vigor.
w084.ex2: The puppy played with so much vigor that she wore us all out.

w085.def: To endure is to keep going through something hard or to last for a long time.
w085.ex1: The Autobots must endure the freezing winds of the northern mountains.
w085.ex2: Strong stone walls can endure for hundreds of years.

w086.def: Terrain is the shape and features of an area of land.
w086.ex1: Rocky terrain slowed the Autobots on their trek across Cybertron.
w086.ex2: Mountain bikes are built for rough terrain.

w087.def: A remote place is very far away from towns and people.
w087.ex1: The Autobots hid their base in a remote canyon.
w087.ex2: We camped in a remote valley with no houses for miles.

w088.def: A vacant place is empty and not being used.
w088.ex1: Wheeljack found a vacant room in the Ark and turned it into a workshop.
w088.ex2: We played soccer in the vacant lot behind the school.

w089.def: Fertile land has rich soil where plants grow well.
w089.ex1: The Autobots planted energon crystals in the fertile valley.
w089.ex2: Farmers love the fertile soil near the river.

w090.def: To inhabit a place is to live there.
w090.ex1: Only a few creatures inhabit the icy mountains near the Autobot base.
w090.ex2: Penguins inhabit the cold lands of Antarctica.

w091.def: An ally is a person or group who helps and supports you, and to ally is to join with others for a goal.
w091.ex1: Optimus Prime thanked his ally for coming to help.
w091.ex2: Small countries sometimes ally with each other to stay strong.

w092.def: A rival is a person or team that competes against you.
w092.ex1: Jazz raced his rival Bumblebee to the top of the hill.
w092.ex2: Our soccer team plays our biggest rival on Saturday.

w093.def: A companion is someone who spends time or travels with you.
w093.ex1: Bumblebee was Optimus Prime's loyal companion on the long trip.
w093.ex2: My dog is my best companion on walks.

w094.def: A citizen is a person who belongs to a country or city and has rights there.
w094.ex1: Every citizen of Iacon cheered when the Autobots returned.
w094.ex2: A good citizen follows the rules and helps the community.

w095.def: A volunteer is a person who offers to do a job without being forced or paid, and to volunteer is to make that offer.
w095.ex1: Ironhide was the first Autobot to volunteer for the rescue.
w095.ex2: Every volunteer at the shelter walked a dog today.

w096.def: To attempt is to try to do something, and an attempt is a try.
w096.ex1: Wheeljack will attempt to fix the engine before nightfall.
w096.ex2: On my third attempt, I finally landed the jump.

w097.def: To persevere is to keep trying even when something is hard.
w097.ex1: Ratchet had to persevere through hours of repair work.
w097.ex2: If you persevere at practicing the piano, you will get better.

w098.def: To strive is to try very hard to do or get something.
w098.ex1: The Autobots strive to protect every living thing they meet.
w098.ex2: I strive to read ten pages every night.
w098.root: Old French estriver — to quarrel, to struggle

w099.def: A diligent person works carefully and steadily.
w099.ex1: The diligent engineer Wheeljack checked every bolt twice.
w099.ex2: Our diligent class cleaned the whole room before recess.

w100.def: A hardship is something that makes life very hard, like losing food or a home.
w100.ex1: The Autobots faced great hardship when they first arrived on a new planet.
w100.ex2: The family faced real hardship during the long winter.

w101.ex1: Cybertron was in great peril when the energon began to run out.
w101.ex2: The hikers were in peril when the storm closed in.
w101.root: Latin periculum — a trial, a danger

w102.def: A vigilant person is watching carefully for danger.
w102.ex1: Ironhide stayed vigilant all night while the others slept.
w102.ex2: Lifeguards must stay vigilant at the pool.

w103.def: A cautious person is careful to avoid danger or mistakes.
w103.ex1: Optimus Prime was cautious as he crept into the dark cave.
w103.ex2: Be cautious when you cross the icy bridge.
w103.root: Latin cautio — cavere (to be on guard)

w104.def: To survive is to stay alive through danger or hardship.
w104.ex1: Few machines could survive the heat of the lava fields on Cybertron.
w104.ex2: Cactus plants survive in the desert with very little water.

w105.def: To evade is to avoid or escape from someone or something, often by clever moves.
w105.ex1: Jazz used his speed to evade the Decepticon scouts.
w105.ex2: The rabbit ran in zigzags to evade the fox.

w106.def: To observe is to watch carefully and notice details.
w106.ex1: Perceptor will observe the stars through his telescope tonight.
w106.ex2: We observe the clouds each morning to track the weather.
w106.root: Latin observare — ob- (toward) + servare (to watch, keep)

w107.def: A glimpse is a quick look at something, and to glimpse is to see something for just a moment.
w107.ex1: Bumblebee caught a glimpse of the Decepticon ship through the clouds.
w107.ex2: We might glimpse a deer through the trees if we stay quiet.

w108.def: To inspect is to look at something closely to check it.
w108.ex1: Ratchet will inspect each Autobot for damage after the long flight.
w108.ex2: The teacher will inspect our science projects before the fair.

w109.def: To scrutinize is to look at something very closely and carefully to find small details.
w109.ex1: Perceptor will scrutinize the map to spot the smallest clue.
w109.ex2: The judge will scrutinize each painting before choosing a winner.
w109.root: Latin scrutari — to search, to examine

w110.ex1: The glowing Autobot symbol was visible from miles away.
w110.ex2: Stars are only visible at night when the sky is clear.

w111.ex1: Energon is essential for every Autobot to stay powered.
w111.ex2: Water is essential for all living things.

w112.def: Something vital is extremely important or necessary for life.
w112.ex1: Wheeljack's message was vital to the Autobots' escape.
w112.ex2: Sleep is vital for a growing body.

w113.def: Something trivial is small and not important.
w113.ex1: Optimus Prime said the dent in his armor was trivial and could wait.
w113.ex2: Do not argue over trivial things like who sits by the window.
w113.root: Latin trivialis — trivium (a place where three roads meet)

w114.def: A priority is something more important than other things that needs to be done first.
w114.ex1: Rescuing the trapped Autobots was Optimus Prime's top priority.
w114.ex2: Finishing homework is my top priority before I play.

w115.def: To emphasize is to give something extra attention to show that it is important.
w115.ex1: Optimus Prime will emphasize that teamwork is the key to winning.
w115.ex2: Our teacher will emphasize the main points before the quiz.

w116.def: Typical means usual or normal for its kind.
w116.ex1: It was a typical day at the Autobot base until a strange light appeared.
w116.ex2: A typical lunch at our school has a sandwich and fruit.
w116.root: Greek typos — a mark or pattern

w117.def: Something peculiar is strange or unusual in an odd way.
w117.ex1: Wheeljack heard a peculiar humming sound inside the old machine.
w117.ex2: The soup had a peculiar taste that nobody could name.

w118.def: A routine is the usual way you do things every day.
w118.ex1: Ratchet's morning routine was to check every Autobot before breakfast.
w118.ex2: My bedtime routine is to brush my teeth, read, and turn out the light.
w118.root: French routine — route (a path, a way)

w119.def: Extraordinary means far beyond what is normal, and amazing.
w119.ex1: Optimus Prime showed extraordinary courage on the battlefield.
w119.ex2: The gymnast's extraordinary leap amazed the crowd.

w120.ex1: Decepticons rarely win a race against Bumblebee.
w120.ex2: It rarely snows in our town, so every flake is exciting.

w121.def: Patient means able to wait calmly, and a patient is also a person getting care from a doctor.
w121.ex1: Optimus Prime stayed patient while Wheeljack finished the long repair.
w121.ex2: The nurse checked on the patient every hour.
w121.root: Latin patiens — pati (to suffer, to endure)

w122.def: A bark is the loud sound a dog makes, and bark is also the rough outer layer of a tree.
w122.ex1: Wheeljack's robot dog gave a loud bark when the Autobots arrived.
w122.ex2: The bark of the old oak tree felt rough under my hand.

w123.def: Fine can mean very good or very thin, and a fine is money you pay as a punishment.
w123.ex1: Jazz did a fine job fixing the engine.
w123.ex2: The driver had to pay a fine for going too fast.

w124.def: A sentence is a group of words that tells a complete thought, and it is also the punishment a judge gives to someone who broke the law.
w124.ex1: Bumblebee wrote one short sentence on the screen to warn the Autobots.
w124.ex2: The judge gave the thief a light sentence.
w124.root: Latin sententia — sentire (to feel, to think)

w125.def: A draft is an early version of something you write, and it is also a stream of cold air in a room.
w125.ex1: Wheeljack finished the first draft of his blueprint last night.
w125.ex2: A cold draft blew in under the door and made me shiver.
w125.root: Old English dragan — to draw, to drag
